title: Telemetry Sink Harmonizer and Schema Healthboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: the Console usage-event pipeline occasionally rejects or misclassifies incoming telemetry due to schema divergence across SDK versions and third‑party integrations. Operators currently lack an at-a-glance view of schema health, and debugging requires repeatedly replaying failed events. This service aims to reduce dropped events, provide richer provenance, and surface schema regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end ingestion drop rate for validated Console usage events falls to <1% for known SDK versions. 2) Schema Healthboard dashboard shows 24-hour and 30-day drift metrics per event type and per-tenant. 3) New Harmonizer adds <=30ms median overhead to request path in steady state. 4) Canary rollout can be enabled per-customer; rollback triggers exist and are tested. 5) Alerts fire when any event type sees >5% invalidates in 15m.
design_notes: Introduce a lightweight Telemetry Sink Harmonizer deployed in the edge ingestion path to: 1) normalize common variant keys (snake_case / camelCase), 2) apply source fingerprinting (sdk_version, platform, route) and stable event type mapping, 3) consult the Schema Registry for per-event contract and decide (strict reject | soft-coerce | accept-with-warning). Keep harmonizer configuration per-tenant via feature flags. Provide a Schema Healthboard service that aggregates validation outcomes, severity tags, and sample payloads (sanitized) for observability. Persist validation summaries to existing telemetry store (usage-events-summary) and surface in Console.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: schema registry integration and normalized mapping table + unit tests. Phase 2: harmonizer middleware with soft-coercion rules and metrics emission. Phase 3: Healthboard UI backend + dashboards and alerting. Phase 4: canary rollout with 2 customers, iterate on coercion rules. Phase 5: global launch and runbook updates.
tasks: Define canonical event shapes and mapping heuristics (engineers + product)
Implement mapping table and plugin point in ingestion proxy
Integrate JSON Schema + Protobuf type resolution in registry client
Implement three-tier validation policy engine (reject, coerce, warn)
Emit validation verdicts and sanitized sample payloads to metrics and S3
Build Healthboard backend endpoints (summaries, drift timeline, per-tenant view)
Add canary feature-flag controls and per-tenant config in console
Add unit/integration tests and chaos tests for backpressure scenarios
monitoring_and_alerting: Emit meter: ingest.harmonizer.latency; counter: ingest.validation.{verdict}; gauge: schema.drift.rate.{event_type}. Create alerts: schema.drift.rate > 5% sustained for 15m, harmonizer.latency.p95 > 150ms, validation.reject_rate > 1% for a tenant over 30m.
performance_targets: Median added latency < 30ms, p95 < 120ms. CPU overhead per harmonizer instance < 8% of current router baseline at 5k rps. Memory overhead capped at +150MB per process.
data_contract_examples: Accepted event example: {"event_type": "session.start", "sdk_version": "1.4.3", "payload": {...}}. Coercible example: timestamp as string -> coerce to ISO; ambiguous numeric fields (stringified ints) -> coerce if within expected bounds. Rejection example: missing required event_type or source_id.
rollout_plan: Start with internal traffic and infra team (1 day). Canary with two customers (1 week each) with feature flag. Monitor metrics and errors; expand to 10% of traffic if stable; full rollout after 2 successful canary cycles. Provide migration window and opt-out by tenant.
migration_strategy: Backfill: do not retroactively mutate stored events. For previously rejected events, provide a replay endpoint and a small transform script to coerce shapes. Communicate changes to customers with SDK guidance and examples.
security_and_compliance: Sanitize all sample payloads before storage; redact PII using existing redaction library. Harmonizer must respect tenant isolation and KMS keys for any persisted sensitive material. Security review required for sample capture and storage flows.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: soft-coercion could mask real client bugs -> Mitigate by pairing coerced events with 'warning' tags and retention of raw payloads for 7 days. Risk: performance regression under burst -> Mitigate with adaptive circuit breaker to bypass harmonizer and tag events for later asynchronous processing.
dependencies_notes: Relies on Schema Registry improvements (ENG-71298) for stable type resolution. Requires console feature-flag infra and UI components (PM-421). Coordination with infra for S3 retention and metrics storage (ENG-30542).
